correctness.rationale: The five-vertex universal claim is certified by complete exact enumeration of all 1,099 labeled graphs, 772 cross-products and 1,099 independent permutation-vs-recursion law checks, from the included verified checker. Enumeration is finite and exhaustive, with mathematical completeness established by the edge-bitmask bijection. For m>=2 the infinite connected family is proved from its maximal-set multiplicities, universal first vertex and star priority, and analytic CDF and likelihood-ratio inequalities. The edge cases and quantifiers are explicit. Computations corroborate rather than replace the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 parking paper uses likelihood-ratio ordering only for an intermediate auxiliary object to prove first-order domination. Testing whether the actual sequential law strengthens ordinary stochastic dominance is therefore naturally motivated. The exact smallest size six, valid across all simple graphs, and the entire connected m>=2 family showing persistent first-order dominance with LR failure identify a sharp structural boundary; this is not a relabeling or arbitrary single-instance counterexample.
